name: Dropdown / Listbox
summary: A styled select is the pattern people reach for and then get wrong — the current value stops being announced, or the arrow keys land on nothing. Here the button, the listbox and every option are real markup you can read and copy, and the script only opens it, moves focus, and remembers what you chose.
demoNote: The panel anchors to its trigger at every width, and flips above it when there is no room below. For a panel that rises from the bottom of the screen, see the Drawer component. This one needs JavaScript; Native Select is the answer when that is not on offer.

contract.useWhen: A custom select, for when the native one cannot be styled the way you need. Needs JavaScript.
keyboard: open it, or choose the focused option
close, then tab on from the trigger
jump to the first option starting with it
failureModes: aria-activedescendant rather than real DOM focus, unreliable on iOS VoiceOver and TalkBack
the trigger named by its label alone, so the current value is never announced
a hidden <select> behind it, so one value lives in two places and they drift
a disabled option left with a tabindex, so the keyboard lands on something inert
a div as the trigger, so aria-expanded sits on something with no role
api: AC.createDropdown(root) -> { open, close, isOpen, value, setValue, refresh, element, destroy }
